item.title: The role of social capital in knowledge management
item.content:encoded:
This special issue explores the interconnection between social capital and knowledge management in organizations. Social capital—networks of relationships, trust, and shared norms—facilitates knowledge exchange and integration, enhancing intellectual capital development and organizational competitiveness across sectors including technology, finance, healthcare, and creative industries.

The call addresses critical research gaps including the lack of general theory explaining how social capital translates to intellectual capital across different contexts, inconsistent measurement approaches, and limited longitudinal studies. It seeks contributions examining how social capital functions as a mediating mechanism in digital environments, how it evolves over time, and how cultural and technological factors influence these dynamics.

The special issue invites empirical and theoretical research from academics and practitioners investigating social capital's role in knowledge creation, innovation outcomes, and competitive advantage, with particular attention to measurement frameworks, trust mechanisms, and organizational structures that enable effective knowledge management.

Appel publié par VINE Journal of Information and Knowledge Management Systems. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • How does social capital translate into intellectual capital across different organizational contexts?
  • In what ways does social capital act as a mediator of knowledge management in digital and dynamic environments?
  • How can social capital in knowledge management be measured? To what extent do trust, networks, and norms function as distinct versus overlapping dimensions of social capital?
  • How does social capital evolve over time, and what are its long-term effects on knowledge creation and sharing?
  • How do individual employee networks aggregate to create firm-level intellectual capital?
  • How is social capital value disclosed?
  • How do national cultures influence the relationship between social capital and knowledge management?
  • In what ways do organizational structures influence the effectiveness of social capital in enabling knowledge management?
  • How do emerging technologies impact the development and role of social capital in knowledge management?
  • What role does trust play in knowledge sharing and knowledge application processes?
  • How can organizations foster trust to strengthen social capital in virtual and hybrid workplaces?
  • How does social capital-driven knowledge management contribute to organizational innovation?
  • What is the relationship between social capital, knowledge management, and competitive advantage in dynamic markets?

Timeline

  • April 1, 2026: Opening date for manuscript submissions
  • October 31, 2026: Closing date for manuscript submissions

This special issue invites research exploring the evolving landscape of crowdfunding as both a financing mechanism and investment vehicle. The call seeks to understand how crowdfunding is changing and will change in the future, particularly considering technological advancements and their differential impacts across crowdfunding models.

Submissions should address topics spanning the complete crowdfunding lifecycle, from venture development and investor performance through post-investment relationships, as well as broader themes including sustainability, internationalization, regulatory developments, and the role of academic institutions. The special issue welcomes contributions from diverse disciplinary and methodological perspectives that shed light on opportunities and challenges within the crowdfunding ecosystem.

item.title: Entrepreneurship, Creative Destruction, and Growth: Enriching the Aghion-Howitt Tradition
item.content:encoded:

Martin Andersson, Blekinge Institute of Technology

David B. Audretsch, Indiana University

Maksim Belitski, University of Reading

Pontus Braunerhjelm, KTH Royal Institute of Technology

This special issue seeks to advance Schumpeterian research that integrates entrepreneurial activities across multiple levels of analysis. It focuses on connecting individual entrepreneurs and firms with regional innovation ecosystems and industrial dynamics, while also considering broader institutional and policy frameworks.

The issue welcomes research on the full lifecycle of ventures, including formation, growth, contraction, and failure, with particular emphasis on how these dynamics drive productivity improvements. It also invites studies that enrich the Aghion-Howitt growth model with contemporary entrepreneurship research insights.

item.title: Capturing Value in the Digital Era: Organizing for Innovation Protection and Information Security
item.content:encoded:
R&D Management has a rich publication history in research on appropriability, intellectual capital and capturing value from innovation. This special issue seeks to update and extend that tradition by explicitly bringing together two adjacent but typically separated conversations.

The first conversation conceptualizes protection of innovation in relation to appropriability mechanisms such as patents, trade secrecy, licensing, contracting, complementary assets, and ecosystem governance to investigate value capture potential.

The second conversation - so far mainly happening in information systems and engineering journals - conceptualizes protection of innovation as information security, such as the protection of R&D artifacts, risks of leakage and theft, industrial espionage, and applications of organizational secrecy for R&D purposes.

Appel publié par R and D Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Appropriability mechanisms such as patents, trade secrecy, licensing, contracting, complementary assets, and ecosystem governance
  • Value capture potential from innovation
  • Protection of R&D artifacts
  • Risks of leakage and theft in innovation
  • Industrial espionage
  • Organizational secrecy for R&D purposes
  • Information security in innovation management
  • Intellectual capital and capturing value from innovation

Timeline

  • April 30, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Novel Forms and Models of Organization
item.content:encoded:
Masatoshi Kato, Kwansei Gakuin University

David Audretsch, Indiana University

Roy Thurik, Erasmus University Rotterdam

Maksim Belitski, University of Reading

Alex Coad, Waseda Business School

Eric Liguori, Florida State University

This special issue examines how firms organize and grow to achieve exceptional performance in response to rapid technological change, globalization, and increasing interconnectedness. The collection focuses on novel organizational forms—such as hidden champions, niche leaders, scaleups, and blitzscalers—that enable firms of different sizes and ages to approach the innovation and productivity frontier while maintaining efficiency and resilience.

The issue welcomes research investigating organizational structures, processes, and governance models that allow firms to outperform competitors across regions, industries, and economic contexts. Particular emphasis is placed on understanding how firms balance internal capabilities with external partnerships, adopt digital technologies, orchestrate global value chains, and navigate policy environments. Research is encouraged from diverse geographic contexts beyond traditional OECD and Western-focused perspectives, including emerging Asian economies and developing regions.

Appel publié par Journal of Small Business Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

  • Digitalization, AI, and process organization (resilience, productivity, and scaling)
  • Ecosystem embedment, alliances, and global value chain orchestration

item.title: Technology Transfer through Collaboration: Bridging Academia, Policy, and Practice
item.content:encoded:
Maksim Belitski, Loyola University New Orleans

James Cunningham, Newcastle University

Riccardo Fini, University of Bologna

Simon Mosey, University of Nottingham

Phillip H. Phan, Johns Hopkins University

This special collection seeks submissions that investigate technology transfer, entrepreneurship, and innovation through partnerships between academic researchers and external stakeholders such as practitioners and policymakers. The editors recognize that meaningful research in this field often benefits from close collaboration across disciplinary and sectoral boundaries, providing access to emerging phenomena and underexplored mechanisms that traditional approaches might miss.

The collection particularly welcomes papers co-authored by academics and non-academic partners including technology transfer professionals, policymakers, entrepreneurs, investors, and innovation intermediaries. Such collaborative work is expected to generate unique insights, improve data access, broaden empirical scope, and tackle fundamental questions from diverse perspectives while maintaining rigorous academic standards.

Appel publié par The Journal of Technology Transfer. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

item.title: Contemporary research in financial technology (Fintech)
item.content:encoded:
Rainer Alt, Leipzig University

Rob Gleasure, Copenhagen Business School

Ke-Wei Huang, National University of Singapore

Mingfeng Lin, Georgia Institute of Technology

De Liu, University of Minnesota

Liudmila Zavolokina, University of Lausanne

FinTech emerged as a disruptive force in the financial industry around 2010, introducing innovative applications and business models. Now an established sector, FinTech has revolutionized payment, financing, lending, and insurance through platform-based, customer-oriented, and crowd-based processes. On the one hand, FinTech solutions have reached a maturity, which is characterized by well-adopted solutions that have reached a critical mass as well as by a growing degree of regulation. In practice, investments in FinTech start-up ventures have decreased and much research has also been published with four special issues in the Electronic Markets journal alone. On the other hand, ongoing technological advancements like agentic and generative artificial intelligence, blockchain/distributed ledger technologies, and quantum computing are driving further innovations.

Appel publié par Electronic Markets. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Interaction and integration between FinTech and traditional financial institutions (e.g., traditional banks, central banks, and central bank digital currencies)
  • Study of segments of FinTech (InsurTech, PropTech, RegTech, Green FinTech and sustainable finance)
  • Research on innovation processes in FinTech and analysis of (new) business models (e.g., crowd-based, digital platforms, decentralized business models)
  • Upcoming concepts in Fintech (e.g., embedded, contextual, silent, open and ubiquitous finance and banking)
  • Use of centralized (e.g., core banking/insurance systems) and decentralized digital platforms (e.g., blockchain and distributed ledger technology) for financial services
  • Research on cryptocurrencies, crypto exchanges, and digital assets (e.g., tokenization, Initial Coin and Securitized Token Offerings (ICO/STO))
  • Emerging standards in the financial industry (e.g., data/process standards and application programming interfaces) and regulations like PSD in Europe
  • Adoption and business value of FinTech models and applications (e.g., financial inclusion and literacy, regulation and governance, diffusion and network effects)
  • Emerging FinTech topics and applications (e.g., quantum computing, metaverse, Internet of Things, Agentic and Generative AI)
  • Studies of innovative applications in FinTech (e.g., robo-advising, algorithmic trading, portfolio management, market making, and social trading)
  • Innovative payment models and systems (e.g., payment networks, micropayments, mobile payments)

item.title: Large Language Models as Methodological Innovators: Advancing Theory and Practice in Technology Management
item.content:encoded:
This special issue seeks to explore how Large Language Models (LLMs) are transforming methodological approaches in technology management research. We invite submissions that demonstrate innovative applications of LLMs as research tools, methodological enhancers, and theoretical instruments for advancing our understanding of technology management, innovation, and organizational change.

Contributions should address both the opportunities and challenges of incorporating LLMs into research practice, including questions of validity, reliability, ethical considerations, and the development of new theoretical frameworks that account for LLM capabilities and limitations in research contexts.

item.title: Knowledge Management despite Resource and Institutional limitations: Advancing Innovation, Resilience, and Organizational Learning
item.content:encoded:
Guillermo Antonio Dávila, Universidad de Lima

Susanne Durst, Bangkok University

Organizations in resource-constrained and institutionally weak contexts face significant challenges in maintaining competitiveness and innovation amid political uncertainty and technological change. This special issue addresses the underexamined role of knowledge management in enabling these organizations—including SMEs, NGOs, and entities in developing regions—to overcome financial constraints, limited technological access, and skilled workforce shortages.

Knowledge management has demonstrated capacity to enhance innovation, strengthen organizational resilience, and foster learning even under severe resource limitations. While empirical evidence from emerging economies supports these benefits, research remains concentrated on stable, well-developed environments, leaving underrepresented contexts insufficiently studied despite their numerical significance and potential for theoretical contribution.

Appel publié par Knowledge Management Research & Practice. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • KM as an enabler of organizational performance under conditions of resource scarcity
  • Knowledge risk management as crucial function in environments characterized by internal and external constraints
  • KM in underrepresented organisational settings, including SMEs, family businesses, informal organisations, low-technology firms, social organisations or geographically isolated regions
  • Organisational learning processes in contexts characterised by institutional and resource constraints
  • The role of KM in strengthening organisational resilience during internal and external crises and disruptions
  • Necessary conditions and bottlenecks for organizational development empowered by KM
  • The interplay between artificial intelligence and KM in overcoming organisational and institutional constraints
  • The role of institutional ecosystems and inter-organisational networks in enhancing the effectiveness of KM
  • Novel methodological approaches for studying KM in constrained and underrepresented contexts

Timeline

  • March 15, 2027: Manuscript deadline

item.title: Beyond the Code: Understanding How, When and Why Humans Employ Generative AI in Innovation
item.content:encoded:
William Y. Degbey, University of Vaasa

Maria Pajuoja, University of Vaasa

Matti Pihlajamaa, VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland

Baniyelme D. Zoogah, McMaster University

Waymond Rodgers, University of Texas

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is defined as the frontier of computational advancements that references human intelligence in addressing ever more complex decision-making problems. A key development is Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen AI), particularly Large Language Models (LLMs) like ChatGPT, which can process and generate human-like language, extract insights, and produce creative outputs. Gen AI has enormous potential to significantly boost national economies. Its widespread adoption could increase GDP in the EU region by +8% (EUR 1.2–1.4 trillion) over the next ten years, provided innovators are equipped with the necessary skills and capabilities.

Yet, adoption remains uneven. For instance, European countries average a 54 percent adoption rate, below the global average of 61 percent. This uneven adoption is compounded by the global competition for skilled talent and persistent workforce shortages, particularly in digital and AI-related fields. McKinsey estimates that up to 12 million job transitions may be required due to AI, underscoring the urgent need for reskilling and entrepreneurial innovation.

Appel publié par Journal of Managerial Psychology. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • How is Gen AI being used in innovation processes at different levels?
  • How do organizations apply Gen AI to replace, reinforce, or reveal innovation activities, and what are the resulting effects on, for example, process efficiency, novelty, and responsiveness to market needs?
  • How do varied patterns of Gen AI use across process phases and organizational levels influence the dynamics and management of innovation processes?
  • How do individual innovators use Gen AI in their work, what influences this usage, and what are the measurable outcomes of AI-augmented innovation efforts in terms of product, service, or process quality and speed?
  • In what ways does Gen AI influence innovation team dynamics, including collaboration, resilience, and decision-making, particularly in virtual or hybrid team environments?
  • What psychological and behavioral effects emerge from using Gen AI in innovation settings, such as changes in employee engagement, collaboration dynamics, or perceptions of autonomy?
  • How do managerial competencies influence the successful implementation of Gen AI in organizational innovation efforts?
  • What organizational capabilities need to be developed to successfully implement, integrate, and support the use of Gen AI in innovation efforts?
  • How are organizations supporting continuous learning and skill development for employees working with Gen AI, and what mechanisms are most effective in enabling the strategic use of Gen AI?
  • What ethical challenges do organizations face when deploying Gen AI in innovation activities, and how are they addressing issues such as intellectual property, transparency, and sociocultural responsibility?

Timeline

  • January 15, 2026: Opening date for manuscripts submissions
  • August 31, 2026: Closing date for manuscripts submission

item.title: Essay Frontiers: A Call for Bold Ideas, New Voices, and New Directions in Logistics and SCM
item.content:encoded:
Maciel Queiroz, FGV EAESP

Morgane Fritz, Excelia Business School

Britta Gammelgaard, University of Southern Denmark

Logistics and supply chain management (L/SCM) have advanced through analytical rigor and empirical refinement. However, the contemporary landscape, shaped by geopolitical shifts, digital transformation, climate pressures, and evolving societal expectations, requires more than incremental extensions of existing models. It calls for a reconsideration of the assumptions, values, and conceptual boundaries that underpin the field. Many of the most pressing challenges in L/SCM today are not only empirical, but also normative, philosophical, and inherently interdisciplinary.

This special issue seeks essays that move beyond established paradigms and offer reflective, provocative, and conceptually grounded perspectives that offer new lenses and open new directions for research and practice. The objective is to complement empirical work by fostering ideas that challenge, reframe, and extend our understanding of L/SCM.

Appel publié par The International Journal of Logistics Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Algorithmic management and the reconfiguration of work in logistics
  • Supply chains as political and strategic infrastructures
  • Entrepreneurial supply chains in contexts of institutional fragility
  • Efficiency versus dignity: ethical boundaries of automation
  • Decolonizing supply chain theory and practice
  • Beyond resilience: strategic adaptation, transformation, and fragility
  • Platformization and ecosystem competition in logistics
  • Invisible labor and precarity in digitally mediated supply chains
  • Sustainability, legitimacy, and organizational narratives
  • The role of human resources in supply chain management
  • Temporal trade-offs: speed, flexibility, and human well-being
  • Culture, identity, and coordination in global supply networks
  • Human–AI collaboration and decision authority in SCM
  • Moral responsibility and accountability in complex supply networks
  • Business model innovation in circular and regenerative supply chains
  • Reimagining SCM theory: integration, borrowing, or paradigm shift?
